item.title: Okayama Fruit Picking: White Peaches and Muscat — Guide
item.description: Because Okayama is Japan’s Fruit Kingdom, picking your own is one of the most enjoyable things to do here in season. Orchards in Akaiwa and the surrounding hills open from early summer for white peaches and from late summer into autumn for Muscat of Alexandria and Shine Muscat grapes. The usual format is a fixed-price session in the greenhouse or orchard, with an all-you-can-eat window of around 30 to 60 minutes, and the option to buy additional fruit to take away.

item.title: Okayama White Peaches & Muscat Grapes: The Fruit Kingdom — Guide
item.description: Okayama’s mild, dry climate and long sunshine hours have made it Japan’s ‘Fruit Kingdom’, and two products define it. The hakuto white peach is grown in paper bags to keep the skin pale and the flesh almost white, producing an intensely perfumed, delicate fruit so soft it is often eaten with a spoon. The Muscat of Alexandria, cultivated in greenhouses here since the Meiji era, yields huge, pale-green, seeded grapes with a distinctive floral aroma, alongside the newer seedless Shine Muscat.
